The pacing of the story is masterfully balanced and mirrors the rhythm of the ferry itself. The narrative mostly unfolds in near "real-time," matching the literal four-minute crossings of the river. Within this short span of story time, the author skillfully compresses thirty-five years of Ilse's life and routine into brief, organic observations (the familiar ache in her back, the recurring Tuesday passenger, the unchanging cold of the river). At the end of the story, time is subtly stretched during the ringing of the telephone; the few seconds it takes for the phone to ring out are drawn out through Ilse's internal reflections about Jonas, effectively building quiet tension and emotional weight before the final line.
